newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end higher boosted by US stocks.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end higher boosted by US stocks.

text.p: Italian shares ended firmer on Wednesday reversing yesterday's sharp losses taking their lead from the surge in the Dow Jones in early trading, firmer European bourses and the steady recovery in domestic bonds.

Dealers said that the market's correction of early this week had largely run its course and stocks were looking to follow other bourses higher, with worries over a delay in the European single currency put on the backburner for now.
The all-share Mibtel index ended up 1.15 percent at 14,805 and the blue chip Mib30 of Italy's top stocks 1.25 percent higher at 22,512.

Olivetti reversed recent losses to end up 9.49 percent at 646 lire boosted by first half results from Omnitel which showed sales up 178 percent and a gross operating margin of seven billion lire. It added it was on track to breakeven in 1998.

Other blue chips moved higher such as ENI, Pirelli, Parmalat and Montedison, but Fiat only ended up 0.31 percent at 6,069 lire despite the government extending Italy's car incentive buying scheme for another 10 months.
Ambroveneto ended up 3.23 percent at 9,861 lire, and after the market closed it announced it had finalised its merger with Cariplo and detailed its 6.5 trillion lire capital increase.

Also among the banks, investment banking group IMI closed up 0.31 percent at 17,531 lire after the company announced late Tuesday first half 1997 net profits at the parent company level up 16 percent at 239 billion lire.
